claims.statement: The EU Energy Efficiency Directive calls for measures encouraging utilization of industrial waste heat where assessment finds benefits exceed costs, and specifies installation-level analysis for certain facilities.

contrary_evidence: The cited framework is conditional on positive cost-benefit analysis and allows exemptions in some circumstances.
Policy encouragement does not establish a bankable source, offtaker, tariff, or pipeline route.

economics.acquisition_route: Energy auditors and direct, data-led outreach to industrial sites and municipal heat operators
economics.founder_net_worth_path: A possible path is several annual project closings plus a retained royalty book that supports multi-million-PLN recurring cash flow and platform value
economics.founder_time: Initially 12-20 hours per week, with engineering and transaction specialists contracted by stage
economics.gross_margin_basis: Expected 55-75% on origination fees after engineering and legal diligence; royalty margin could be higher
economics.payback: Unknown; one closed project could repay setup, but sales cycles may exceed two years
economics.pricing: Unvalidated: 100000-500000 PLN development fee per closed project plus 1-3% of heat revenue or project value
economics.retention_or_repeat: Each project is long-cycle, while royalties and repeat portfolios could provide durable revenue

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: An exclusive heat-source catalogue, local thermal map, contract templates, and buyer relationships improve with every originated site
fingerprint.customer: District-heating operators, greenhouse developers, industrial heat users, and infrastructure investors
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Industrial energy auditors, municipal heating planners, regional economic zones, and targeted geospatial heat-demand mapping
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Source options, temperature and load screening, offtaker matching, standardized diligence, and transaction coordination without initially financing pipes or heat pumps
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The buyer or project company pays a development fee at feasibility or financial close and an optional royalty on delivered heat
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A facility or heating plan identifies potentially usable waste heat but lacks a counterparty and project developer

founder_fit: Uses quantitative geospatial screening and energy knowledge
Can begin as rights origination without owning infrastructure
Polish regional and renewable-energy contacts provide an initial wedge
Project specialists can be hired instead of building a large technical team immediately
risks: Long cycles can consume founder time before revenue
Exclusive rights may be worthless if heat quality or demand is poor
Utilities and industrial owners may resist intermediary economics
Permitting, easements, counterparty credit, and capex can kill projects

structure.control_point: Exclusive commercialization rights over identified waste-heat streams
structure.critical_dependency: A source and offtaker must be close enough, technically compatible, financeable, and willing to sign long-term contracts

thesis: Sign exclusive, time-limited rights to market unused heat from factories, wastewater facilities, and data centres, map nearby demand, and earn development fees and royalties when a district-heating, greenhouse, or industrial offtake project closes.
title: Industrial Waste-Heat Commercialization Rights Bank
uncertainties: Unknown number of financeable source-offtaker pairs in reachable Polish regions
Unknown willingness to grant exclusivity before feasibility
No engineering cost curve or buyer pricing has been validated
Polish heat-market and municipal procurement constraints need counsel
